2013_055_101513spmtg.paragraph: Special meeting agenda of the Board of Trustees of the Troy School District for October 15, 2013 at 5:00 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, carrying two items: a Memorandum of Understanding with the Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program of Southfield and a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c). The MOU commences October 15, 2013, renews annually, and is terminable on sixty (60) days notice. Most consequentially, it designates WOT an “other school official” and commits the Board to provide personally identifiable student information by October 15, 2013; no fees are due by either party.

**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Board of Trustees, Troy School District, October 15, 2013, 5:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; phone 248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Agenda: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Other — Women of Tomorrow ‘Memo of Understanding’; 4. Closed Session — Negotiations; 5. Adjournment. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

**Item 3.A — Women of Tomorrow MOU**
The program’s mission is to inspire, motivate and empower at-risk young women through mentoring by highly accomplished professional women and scholarship opportunities. The recommended action is a resolution to sign the attached agreement.

| Element | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Parties | Troy School Board, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Ml 48098; Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program, Detroit Metropolitan Area, Inc. (WOT-Metro Detroit), 17251 West 12 Mile Road, Suite 204, Southfield, MI 48076 |
| Date | Executed the 15th day of October, 2013; program commencing October 2013 |
| Term | Automatically renews annually; terminable by either party on sixty (60) days prior written notice |
| Founder | Jennifer Valoppi, author and television journalist |
| Fees | None due by either party; scholarships paid directly to students at WOT’s sole discretion |

**Student data**
The Board designates WOT an “other school official” so it may receive personally identifiable Student Information — name, grade level, date of birth, social security number, school attending, academic performance, attendance, grades and standardized test scores, health data, family background, counselor ratings, and verified reports of serious or recurrent behavior patterns — and agrees to provide it by October 15, 2013. WOT may share it with third-party providers, use de-identified data for research, and owns any aggregated data and resulting intellectual property. WOT must comply with FERPA.

**Responsibilities**
WOT recruits volunteer Mentors who meet a small group (10 - 15) of at-risk young women (“Mentees”) once a month for at least one (1) hour per month during the school day on school grounds, under District supervision; it also trains Mentors, staffs a WOT Program Coordinator, arranges career field trips and college visits, and retains fiscal control. The Board secures participating high schools and consents, selects students, names a WOT School Coordinator, provides space, runs background checks, pays all field trip and college visit costs, and assigns an official to attend all program meetings and carry legal reporting obligations (incest, Mentee abuse, evidence of a crime); WOT is never required to make such reports.

**Insurance and disputes**
WOT must carry Workers’ Compensation with Employers Liability; Commercial General Liability on an occurrence basis at not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence; Motor Vehicle Liability at not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence; and Professional Liability at not less than $1,000,000 per claim, naming the School Board, its officials, employees and volunteers as primary Additional Insureds, with thirty (30) days notice of cancellation to Dr. Barbara Fowler and renewal certificates at least (10) days before expiration. Disputes go to Oakland County Circuit Court, the 52nd-4th District Court, or arbitration under Chapter 50 of the Revised Judicature Act administered by the American Arbitration Association, one arbitrator or three where a claim exceeds $1,000,000; MCL §600.5001 et seq. applies.

**Item 4.A — Closed Session**
A resolution is required to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, as permitted by Public Act 267, Section 8(c); no business follows other than adjournment. Roll call listing: Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart. Signature blocks: Nancy Philippart, President, Troy Board of Education, and Jennifer Valoppi, President & Founder.

**Meeting notice and agenda**
The Board of Trustees of the Troy School District noticed a special meeting for October 15, 2013 beginning at 5:00 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The cover carries phone 248.823.4000 and www.troy.k12.mi.us. When school is in session, Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and may be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The five agenda items are: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Other — Consideration: Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program ‘Memo of Understanding’; 4. Closed Session — Consideration: Negotiations; and 5. Adjournment. A repeated footnote states that all meetings except closed sessions are open, that public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, that each person may speak up to three minutes, that the President may reduce the limit when speakers exceed the time available, and that no one’s right to address the Board will be denied. Items need not be taken in the order shown.

**Item 3.A — Women of Tomorrow MOU**
The board memo, tabbed 3. A. 10.15.13, describes the Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program as an organization whose mission is to inspire, motivate and empower at-risk young women to live up to their full potential through a unique mentoring program with highly accomplished professional women and scholarship opportunities. The recommended action is adoption of a resolution to sign the attached agreement, with blank “Moved by” and “Supported by” lines.

The MOU is between the Troy School Board, whose address is 4400 Livernois, Troy, Ml 48098, and the Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program, Detroit Metropolitan Area, Inc. (WOT-Metro Detroit), whose address is 17251 West 12 Mile Road, Suite 204, Southfield, MI 48076, entered into on the 15th day of October, 2013 to implement the WOT program commencing in October of 2013. The recitals state that WOT is designed to meet the needs of at-risk teenage girls in the nation’s public high schools; that both parties believe the program benefits Troy School District students; that it was founded and headed by Jennifer Valoppi, author and television journalist; and that both want WOT to be an official School Board program.

**Term and student information (Section B)**
The Agreement commences October 15, 2013, automatically renews annually until amended or terminated, and may be terminated by either party upon sixty (60) days prior written notice. The School Board designates WOT an “other school official” or applicable state equivalent, including the ability to receive personally identifiable student information. The enumerated Student Information covers name, grade level, date of birth, social security number, school attending, academic performance, attendance, academic work completed, level of achievement records including grades and standardized achievement test scores, attendance data, scores on standardized intelligence, aptitude and psychological tests, health data, family background information, teacher or counselor ratings and observations, and verified reports of serious or recurrent behavior patterns. The Board agrees to provide it by October 15, 2013, recognizing WOT’s legitimate educational interest in operating its programs and researching effectiveness. WOT may pass the information to third-party providers, may use de-identified Student Data for research, and owns any aggregated data and any inventions, patents or other intellectual property created from it.

**Roles of WOT (Section C)**
WOT will recruit Mentors and secure their commitment to meet with a small group (10 - 15) of at-risk young women (“Mentees”) once a month for at least one (1) hour per month throughout the school year, on school grounds during the school day. Mentors are volunteers, not WOT employees, and must be under School District personnel supervision at all times they are with students. WOT will orient and train Mentors with school personnel assistance; support its designated WOT Program Coordinator, a WOT employee acting as liaison with the applicable high school(s); coordinate scheduling, career-focused field trips and specialized college campus visits; provide outcome-based evaluations using quantifiable and qualitative goals; retain full management and fiscal control; require Mentors to complete any school volunteer application and undergo a background check conducted by the School Board; specify program criteria and Mentor activities; and provide criteria for defining at-risk young women.

**Roles of the School Board (Section D)**
The Board will secure participation by senior high schools of its choosing, including consents for Mentees to attend during school hours; select and provide students using WOT criteria; identify at least one staff member per high school as “WOT School Coordinator” to collect paperwork and provide administrative support; provide meeting space during the school day; conduct security background checks; assure the service location conforms with State Uniform Building Codes for Public Educational Facilities; assure Mentors are used only for working with students having special needs; assure only the WOT Program Coordinator may reassign or transfer a Mentor between schools or centers; handle all field trip and college visit paperwork and bear all related costs; adhere to all WOT program guidelines absent an express written waiver from WOT’s President; facilitate surveying of students; and assign a School Board official at each participating school to supervise the program and attend all WOT program meetings, responsible for legal reporting obligations such as suspicions of incest, Mentee abuse or evidence of a crime. WOT shall in no event be required to make such reports.

**Fees (Section E)**
No fees or payments are due by either party. Scholarships for qualified students are paid directly to students by the WOT Program, and all scholarship decisions are made at WOT’s sole discretion.

**Indemnification, disputes and insurance (Section F)**
WOT agrees to hold harmless and indemnify the School Board and its members, officers and employees against any claim, action, loss, damage, injury, liability, cost or expense, including attorney’s fees and court costs, arising out of bodily injury or property damage from WOT’s performance; nothing indemnifies the School Board for its own performance failures. Disputes may be settled by suit in Oakland County Circuit Court or the 52nd-4th District Court, or by arbitration if both parties elect, under Chapter 50 of the Revised Judicature Act, administered by the American Arbitration Association with one arbitrator, or three arbitrators where any party’s claim exceeds $1,000,000. Each party bears its own costs and an equal share of arbitrator and administrative fees; arbitration qualifies as statutory arbitration under MCL §600.5001 et seq. and takes place in Oakland County, Michigan; Michigan law governs.

WOT shall not commence work until it obtains, at its sole expense, insurance from carriers licensed and admitted in Michigan and acceptable to the School Board:

| Coverage | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Workers’ Compensation | Including Employers Liability Coverage, per Michigan statutes |
| Commercial General Liability | Occurrence basis, not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence combined single limit for Personal Injury, Bodily Injury and Property Damage; includes Contractual Liability, Products and Completed Operations, Independent Contractors Coverage, Broad Form General Liability Extensions, deletion of Explosion, Collapse and Underground (XCU) Exclusions |
| Motor Vehicle Liability | Including no-fault coverages, not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence combined single limit, covering owned, non-owned and hired vehicles |
| Professional Liability | Not less than $1,000,000 per claim if applicable |

General Liability and Motor Vehicle Liability must add as Additional Insureds the School Board, its elected and appointed officials, employees and volunteers, and all boards, commissions and authorities, with that coverage primary. Policies must carry a “Thirty (30) days Advance Written Notice of Cancellation or Non-Renewal” endorsement directed to Dr. Barbara Fowler, Superintendent of Schools, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. At execution WOT must supply two (2) copies of Certificates of Insurance for each of the four coverages. Renewal certificates are due at least (10) days before expiration; on failure to maintain coverage the School Board may purchase it and subtract the cost from the Agreement amount, with no obligation to procure the most cost-effective coverage.

**Confidentiality and miscellaneous (Sections G and H)**
The School Board acknowledges it will access confidential or proprietary information developed by WOT, including methods, systems and operating procedures, and covenants not to divulge, disclose or copy it during or after the term. Neither party shall discriminate because of race, age, religion, color, gender, national origin, marital status, physical or mental disability, or sexual orientation. Modifications require a written document executed by all parties. WOT shall comply with FERPA and all state and federal student confidentiality laws. Program notices go to Jennifer Valoppi, Founder & President, Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program, Inc., 22 East Flagler Street, 6th Floor, Miami, Florida 33132; notices to the Board go to Dr. Barbara A. Fowler, Superintendent of Schools, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The document may be executed in two (2) or more counterparts. There are no third-party beneficiaries; the Agreement is fully integrated; jurisdiction lies in the State courts of Oakland County, Michigan; the Agreement binds successors and assigns; assignment requires prior written consent except that WOT may assign to a parent, subsidiary or affiliated entity; a Force Majeure clause covers fire, hurricane, earthquake, explosion, wars, sabotage, accident, flood, acts of God, strikes or other labor disputes, riot or civil commotion; severability, captions-for-convenience, signer-authority, independent-contractor and survival clauses follow. Signature blocks are provided for the Troy School Board of Education by Nancy Philippart, President, Troy Board of Education, and for the Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program by Jennifer Valoppi, President & Founder, each with an undated date line.

**Item 4.A — Closed Session on Negotiations**
Tabbed 4. A. 10.15.13, this item states the Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, after which no additional business will take place other than to officially adjourn. The resolution reads: “Be it therefore resolved that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss negotiations.” A roll call vote is called for, with trustees listed as Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, and Philippart; no recorded votes appear in the document.
